summary: Introductory walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on per-route telemetry, cost attribution, and operational controls. Customer liked route filters and cost drilldowns; asked about private deployment, KMS, and latency SLOs. Agreed to run a small dedicated pilot and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-11-19 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Marcus (CTO - Halcyon), Priya (SRE), Omar (Head of ML), Leah (FinOps).

Summary: Quick live demo of the Redwood Console with focus on usage analytics per route, cost slicing per model and per-route, and operational controls (canaries, fallbacks). Customer asks about pilot for Dedicated capacity and compliance artifacts.

[00:00] Samir: Hey team, thanks for carving time today. quick intros — i'm samir redwood ae, elena is our solutions engineer who will drive the console demo. Marcus, wanna kick off with what you're hoping to see?

[00:18] Marcus: Yeah thanks, uh main thing for us is visibility. we have a few different product routes — chat assist, document summarization, and an internal search reranker — and we need per-route billing so product teams can be charged back. We also need low variance latency, like p95 under 200ms for chat.

[00:32] Elena: Great — that's exactly what i'll show. we'll look at the usage lens, then the per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown by model, tokens, and infra. also i'll point out the filters you can set for teams and for environment.

[01:05] [screen-share starts, slight audio blip] Elena: Alright opening the Console... top left is the Usage Overview — this shows overall tokens, requests, errors. you can change the time window — last 24h, 7d, 30d. i'm going to switch to the route view.

[02:02] Elena: Here are the routes — chat-assist, doc-summarize, rerank-search, and a few internal test routes. you can click a route to see per-token cost, token counts, average latency, and 95th latency. note the small cost spike on 11/15 for rerank-search — that's from a bad loop in their client, we often see that.

[03:10] Leah: quick q — how is cost computed? are we charged per-token plus infra overhead? we need to reconcile with our finance system.

[03:20] Elena: Good question. Console shows unit economics broken down into Model unit costs (per-token based on the model and quantization profile), Runtime infra allocation (a share of GPU-hours per route based on throughput and KV cache hits), and additional services like embeddings/ops. we provide both estimated direct cost and an allocated infra cost so you can do internal chargebacks. you can export CSVs or push to your billing system via webhooks.

[04:05] Priya: How accurate is the infra allocation? we have bursty traffic — we can't have finance surprised by big infra charges.

[04:20] Elena: The allocation uses moving-window utilization and counts reserved vs burst capacity. for Dedicated pools you get a deterministic allocation — if you reserve N slots you see per-route assigned capacity. For Hosted we use a cost-proxy model that estimates based on token volumes, batching efficiency, and observed GPU utilization. it's not perfect but it's within typical ±5-10% of actual.

[05:02] Samir: Also note our Optimize recommendations — if batching or prefix caching would drop token egress by 20% we'll show projected savings, you can simulate it in the console.

[05:28] Omar: Tell me more about caching — we have repeated prefixes in chat, will that help?

[05:36] Elena: Yes, we do prefix and KV cache. prefix caching handles repeated initial tokens and KV cache reduces costs for continuation tokens by reusing cached key/value states. in the Console you'll see cache hit rates per route — here rerank-search has low cache; chat-assist shows 37% KV hit which explains lower token spend.

[06:10] [timestamp jump — 1-2s cut] Marcus: If we enable Private (VPC), does the console still show the metrics?

[06:22] Elena: Yes — the control plane remains similar. For Private deployments we ingest telemetry via a secure collector (or on-prem agent) and the Console surface is near identical. we also support on-prem packaging for air-gapped setups; some fields like raw token payloads are redacted/never leave your network when requested.

[07:00] Priya: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML, SCIM, and per-route ACLs so only product teams can view their routes.

[07:12] Samir: We support SAML SSO, SCIM user sync, and fine-grained roles. you can bind teams to routes and enforce read-only on others. plus all actions are logged to audit logs with request ids for traceability.

[07:48] [Elena clicks into chat-assist route detail] Elena: seeing the route detail — top right is a cost timeline. you can drill into a specific day and see breakdown by model variant, tokens, and runtime allocation. below is a latency distribution chart and below that are top tokens by cost.

[08:35] Leah: top tokens — that's interesting, is that raw token text? we need PII controls.

[08:42] Elena: we surface token metadata but we can configure redaction. by default sensitive text is hashed/anonymized. you can also opt-out of storing token-level payloads entirely.

[09:12] Jonas: i'll show the route filters — you can tag routes with product, environment, and owner. then the usage lens lets you slice by tag. here's an example: filter to product=mobile and show cost per route; you can allocate percentages for chargeback if a route is shared.

[10:02] [timestamp 10:02] Marcus: A couple of objections — first, latency variance. hosted is cheaper but dedicated seems necessary for strict SLOs. what's the switching story if we start hosted and then move to Dedicated?

[10:18] Elena: Migration is straightforward. routing policies let you pin a route to hosted or dedicated pools; we have automated warmup for KV caches and model variant fallbacks to avoid cold starts. many customers pilot in hosted, then ramp to Dedicated. we also support hybrid: critical routes on Dedicated, bulk background routes on hosted.

[11:05] Priya: About encryption — do you integrate with KMS / HSM? we have strict key control requirements.

[11:15] Samir: yes — KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private, customer-managed keys in the Private product, and we support HSM-backed signing for audit logs.

[11:40] Omar: Any regulatory certifications? we need SOC2 type 2, and some clients ask for ISO27001.

[11:50] Samir: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 in our compliance pack; we'll attach the package after the call. also we provide penetration test reports under NDA.

[12:20] [Elena toggles to the Cost Simulator] Elena: here's the Cost Simulator — you can take your historical traffic, apply different quantization profiles and batching, and get a projected monthly spend. I'm going to run a quick sim: switching the rerank model from fp32 to int8-quantized reduces model unit cost by 45% but increases latency by ~10ms. you can preview accuracy regressions if you upload a small eval set.

[13:38] Leah: That's helpful — our FinOps wants conservative estimates with accuracy regressions called out.

[14:00] Elena: Under Optimize we have a list of recommended actions — e.g., enable KV cache for this route, reduce max tokens on system prompts, or moveheavy reranks to a cheaper model for weekend batch jobs. you can export these recommendations as tickets to Jira.

[15:10] Jonas: One operational feature — canaries and auto-fallback. you can create rollouts that route X% of traffic to a new model or to Dedicated; if latency or error rate crosses thresholds it automatically falls back.

[15:42] Marcus: Do we get tracing back to our services? we have request IDs and want to correlate.

[15:50] Elena: Yep — you can inject trace headers; Redwood traces include request id, route, model-version and cost tags. those appear in the Console's trace view and you can link out to your APM.

[16:20] Priya: One more — retention. how long do logs and tokens hang around? we have data retention rules.

[16:30] Samir: Default retention is 90 days for metrics and 30 days for token-level metadata, but for Private you can set retention to your policy — even zero retention. audit logs retention can be extended as needed for compliance.

[17:05] [short pause, background typing] Elena: Okay i'm going to demo a chargeback report — selecting last month, grouping by owner tag, and exporting a CSV. here's a preview: product A owes $23k, product B $4.2k, rerank-search internal tools $1.1k. you can set monthly budgets and alerts.

[18:12] Leah: Will the alerts tie into Slack or PagerDuty?

[18:18] Elena: Yes, alerting supports Slack, PagerDuty, and webhook sinks. you can create cost alerts (thresholds) and performance SLO alerts.

[19:00] Marcus: About the pilot — what's the minimum commitment for a Dedicated trial and what would you need from us to run a pilot?

[19:10] Samir: For a short Dedicated pilot we usually ask for a 2-week reserved pool at modest scale (config example included in the pilot doc). to run it we need a small sample of your traffic patterns, a target list of critical routes, and an NDA for certain security docs. we can run an on-prem benchmark or a VPC-connected Dedicated pool.

[20:05] Priya: We'll provide traffic histograms and p95 targets. also need to validate KMS integration.

[20:20] Samir: Great. Action items: I'll send the security package and pricing, Elena will share the console short video and route screenshots, Priya will share traffic sample.

[21:00] [Elena demonstrates the audit log export — filename redacted] Elena: here's the audit CSV — each action has a timestamp, user id, IP and request id. we can also stream logs to your SIEM via a secure connector.

[22:12] Omar: quick question on multi-model routing — do you support mixing a lightweight reranker and a larger generator in a single route?

[22:28] Jonas: you can chain calls in our workflow engine or call different model variants as steps. the Console shows end-to-end cost and latency for the whole flow.

[23:05] [small crosstalk, someone drops briefly] Speaker 1: sorry, dropped — back

[23:20] Elena: No worries. final note: you can create saved views for teams, pin their cost dashboards, and set monthly budgets with automatic throttles if needed.

[24:00] Marcus: ok this was useful — next meeting should be technical bench with your infra team and our SREs to validate latency and KMS. can we do that week after next?

[24:12] Samir: Yes, we proposed 11/25 for a bench. I'll send invites.

[24:30] Leah: one more ask — could you share an example of the cost allocation algorithm so our finance folks can audit?

[24:42] Elena: We'll share a short doc: allocation methodology, assumptions, and caveats.

[25:00] [wrap up] Samir: Great — recap: Samir send security pack & pricing, Elena send console video & docs, Priya share traffic histograms, schedule bench on 11/25. thanks everyone.

[25:25] Marcus: Thanks all.

[25:30] [call ends — notes: slight transcription artifacts, some speaker labels generic]
